excerpts.quote: Yields on Treasury nominal securities at “constant maturity” are interpolated by the U.S. Treasury from the daily yield curve for non-inflation-indexed Treasury securities. This curve, which relates the yield on a security to its time to maturity, is based on the closing market bid yields on actively traded Treasury securities in the over-the-counter market. These market yields are calculated from composites of quotations obtained by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. The constant maturity yield values are read from the yield curve at fixed maturities, currently 1, 3, and 6 months and 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 20, and 30 years. This method provides a yield for a 10-year maturity, for example, even if no outstanding security has exactly 10 years remaining to maturity.

facts_not_substitutes.currency: USD; rate ratio units, not USD currency amounts

comparison_contract: CMT from one common observation date; closing bid yield curve interpolation. Compare against forward or trailing equity earnings yield separately and retain vendor period methodology.
1/PE*100 is an accounting earnings-price ratio. Neither forward estimated accounting earnings nor trailing earnings is a bond coupon, distributed cash yield or guaranteed annual equity return.

Earnings yield minus Treasury yield is a descriptive ratio gap, not a complete model-implied equity risk premium. Growth, margins, dilution, retained-earnings reinvestment, payout and equity drawdowns remain separate.
Do not subtract current historical CPI YoY to assert future real return. Breakeven/inflation premium needs same-maturity TIPS model assumptions and is not collected here.

Short duration has lower usual interest-rate price sensitivity but reinvestment exposure. Long duration locks a longer cash-flow term but is more sensitive to yield changes before maturity. Duration is not identical to maturity.

Direct coupon Treasury held to maturity has a nominal USD cash-flow contract; reinvestment of coupons at assumed YTM and credit/default conditions matter for matching realized compound YTM. Coupon-free bills held to maturity avoid coupon reinvestment but maturity rollover is uncertain.
A rolling bond ETF lacks an individual investor bond maturity promise and its distribution/SEC yield is not this CMT value.
KRW investor can lose domestic-currency value even when Treasury meets USD payments. Equities and Treasuries share USD currency exposure; compare economic asset cash flows separately from FX.
